analyst_view.overall: Olympiacos are 6th in the Europa League with 10 points and unbeaten in five European games; AC Milan are 28th with 3 points and need a win in Piraeus to get back towards the play-off places, though they arrive after a 5-1 league win over Frosinone. Leon Bailey is now confirmed out: an MRI on Monday showed a hamstring strain that keeps him out for about three weeks (in.gr, Sportday via Il Milanista), and the numbers do not know about it; Gelson Martins should replace him. The numbers already take off Chiquinho, Hezze, Puerta, El Kaabi and Yazici for Olympiacos and Modric, Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze and the banned Perera for Milan; Italian reports add Pavlovic (kidney colic), Bartesaghi, Camarda and Terracciano, so Amorim has little room to rotate and Maignan returns in goal. English referee Chris Kavanagh's card record is already counted (about +19%). My leans stay small: slightly fewer corners and shots without Bailey, slightly more cards because Milan must chase.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals (1.0 Olympiacos, 1.1 Milan), already cut for Chiquinho and Hezze and for Modric, and nudged up for both sides' recent scoring. Bailey, who scored twice in the 6-2 win over Iraklis, is now confirmed out and the numbers don't know it; Milan missing centre-back Pavlovic works a little the other way, so I trim only slightly, to about 2.06.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.9 corners, 5.3 for Olympiacos, already adding for their busy wide play (+7.8%) and taking off Milan's low recent count. With Bailey's hamstring strain now confirmed by Greek and Italian outlets, Olympiacos lose one of their main wide outlets, something the numbers can't see, so I go a bit lower, to about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, adding about 19% for referee Chris Kavanagh's record and trimming a little for both sides' calm recent games. The referee is counted, so I don't size him again; my small lean to about 5.0 is for the stakes, with Milan needing a win in a full, loud Karaiskakis and Olympiacos chasing a top-eight place.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.7 shots, 15.3 for Olympiacos and 9.4 for Milan, already adding for Olympiacos' busy attack (+9.5%) and cutting Milan for their thin recent output (-16%). Bailey's confirmed absence takes some threat from Olympiacos, while Milan chasing the game works the other way, so I go slightly lower, to about 24.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, with Milan's lower recent accuracy already taken off. Pulisic and Ramos lead Milan's threat and should start after the 5-1 against Frosinone, while Olympiacos lose Bailey, one of their most accurate shooters, and rely on Gelson, Jota Silva and Gonzalez, so I trim a little to about 8.0.
